key_insight: AxiGSIS couples a kinetic discrete-velocity solver with a synthetic macroscopic system to accelerate steady-state simulation of axisymmetric rarefied gas and charged-particle flows.
engineering_relevance: The method can reduce iteration cost and spatial resolution needs for near-continuum to moderate rarefied regimes while preserving accuracy in electrostatic and axisymmetric flow applications.
method: Finite-volume discrete velocity method on a 2D axisymmetric meridian plane with 3D molecular velocity space
Kinetic solver computes nonequilibrium stress and heat flux, then feeds them as corrective sources to the macroscopic synthetic system
Macroscopic primitives are updated rapidly and passed back to the kinetic solver in a bidirectional coupling loop
evidence_signal: The paper evaluates four benchmarks—Taylor Couette flow, neutral nozzle expansion, charged-particle flow past an electrostatic sphere, and electrostatically accelerated charged-particle nozzle flow—and reports agreement with reference kinetic solutions plus fewer cells and iterations.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend on the flow being steady and axisymmetric, so extension to strongly transient or fully 3D configurations may require additional treatment.
paper_title: A general synthetic iterative solver for axisymmetric rarefied gas and electrostatic charged-particle flows
